Preferred Position: Confidentiality limited to specific defined information.
Fallback 1: Confidentiality limited to information explicitly identified in the agreement.
Fallback 2: Confidentiality limited to information provided in writing.
Fallback 3: Confidentiality limited to information shared during meetings.
Red Line: Confidentiality includes all information exchanged during discussions.
Deal Breaker: Confidentiality includes all information, including non-disclosure of sensitive internal processes.

Preferred Position: 30-day written notice period with automatic renewal unless terminated.
Fallback 1: 30-day written notice period with automatic renewal unless terminated.
Fallback 2: 15-day written notice period with automatic renewal unless terminated.
Fallback 3: 7-day written notice period with automatic renewal unless terminated.
Red Line: No notice period required for termination.
Deal Breaker: Termination without notice or penalty.

Preferred Position: Compliance with GDPR and CCPA standards.
Fallback 1: Compliance with GDPR and other applicable data protection laws.
Fallback 2: Compliance with minimum data protection standards.
Fallback 3: Compliance with basic data protection requirements.
Red Line: No data protection obligations imposed on the vendor.
Deal Breaker: Data processing without any legal compliance requirements.

Preferred Position: 72-hour notification of security incidents with full disclosure.
Fallback 1: 48-hour notification of security incidents with partial disclosure.
Fallback 2: 24-hour notification of security incidents with limited disclosure.
Fallback 3: Notification within 12 hours with no disclosure required.
Red Line: No obligation to notify of security incidents.
Deal Breaker: No obligation to notify or remediate security incidents.

Preferred Position: All IP developed during the engagement belongs to the client.
Fallback 1: IP developed during the engagement is owned by the client unless otherwise agreed.
Fallback 2: IP developed during the engagement is owned by the client, with exceptions for third-party IP.
Fallback 3: IP developed during the engagement is owned by the client, with limited exceptions.
Red Line: IP ownership is not specified or transferred.
Deal Breaker: IP ownership remains with the vendor.

Preferred Position: Fixed-price contract with clear deliverables and payment milestones.
Fallback 1: Fixed-price contract with clear deliverables and payment milestones.
Fallback 2: Fixed-price contract with clear deliverables and no payment milestones.
Fallback 3: Fixed-price contract with limited deliverables and no payment milestones.
Red Line: No fixed-price terms or deliverables defined.
Deal Breaker: No contract terms defined or agreed upon.

Preferred Position: AI models are trained on non-sensitive, anonymized data only.
Fallback 1: AI models are trained on non-sensitive data with limited anonymization.
Fallback 2: AI models are trained on non-sensitive data with minimal anonymization.
Fallback 3: AI models are trained on non-sensitive data with no anonymization.
Red Line: AI models are trained on any data without restrictions.
Deal Breaker: AI models are trained on any data, including sensitive and personal information.

Preferred Position: Scope defined in detail with deliverables and timelines.
Fallback 1: Scope defined in detail with deliverables but no timelines.
Fallback 2: Scope defined with general deliverables and timelines.
Fallback 3: Scope defined with limited deliverables and timelines.
Red Line: Scope not defined or agreed upon.
Deal Breaker: No defined scope or deliverables.

Preferred Position: Licensing based on user count with annual renewal options.
Fallback 1: Licensing based on user count with annual renewal options.
Fallback 2: Licensing based on user count with no renewal options.
Fallback 3: Licensing based on user count with limited renewal options.
Red Line: Licensing based on usage with no user count restrictions.
Deal Breaker: Licensing based on usage with no user count or renewal options.

Preferred Position: Data stored within the EU and subject to EU data protection laws.
Fallback 1: Data stored within the EU or other specified regions.
Fallback 2: Data stored within the EU or other regions with minimal restrictions.
Fallback 3: Data stored within the EU or other regions with no restrictions.
Red Line: Data stored outside of the EU with no restrictions.
Deal Breaker: Data stored anywhere without restrictions.

Preferred Position: Confidentiality obligations apply to all disclosed information, including trade secrets, and remain in effect for 5 years.
Fallback 1: Confidentiality obligations apply to all disclosed information, including trade secrets, and remain in effect for 3 years.
Fallback 2: Confidentiality obligations apply to all disclosed information, but the duration is negotiable.
Fallback 3: Confidentiality obligations apply only to information explicitly marked as confidential.
Red Line: Confidentiality obligations do not apply to any information disclosed during the term of the agreement.
Deal Breaker: Confidentiality obligations do not apply to any information and the other party is not bound by any duty of confidentiality.

Preferred Position: Customer retains ownership of all data processed by the SaaS platform, including derivative data.
Fallback 1: Customer retains ownership of all data processed by the SaaS platform, including derivative data, but the provider may retain copies for backup purposes.
Fallback 2: Customer retains ownership of all data processed by the SaaS platform, but the provider may retain copies for backup purposes.
Fallback 3: Customer retains ownership of all data processed by the SaaS platform, but the provider may retain copies for operational use.
Red Line: Customer does not retain ownership of any data processed by the SaaS platform.
Deal Breaker: Customer does not retain ownership of any data and the provider owns all data processed through the platform.

Preferred Position: The agreement applies to all data processing activities, including third-party data transfers and subprocessing.
Fallback 1: The agreement applies to all data processing activities, including third-party data transfers, but not subprocessing.
Fallback 2: The agreement applies to all data processing activities, but subprocessing is subject to additional approval.
Fallback 3: The agreement applies to all data processing activities, but subprocessing is not explicitly covered.
Red Line: The agreement does not apply to any data processing activities outside of the initial scope.
Deal Breaker: The agreement does not apply to any data processing activities and the provider is not bound by any obligations.

Preferred Position: The provider must notify the customer of any security incident within 24 hours and provide a detailed incident report within 7 days.
Fallback 1: The provider must notify the customer of any security incident within 48 hours and provide a detailed incident report within 14 days.
Fallback 2: The provider must notify the customer of any security incident within 72 hours and provide a detailed incident report within 30 days.
Fallback 3: The provider must notify the customer of any security incident within 7 days and provide a detailed incident report within 60 days.
Red Line: The provider is not required to notify the customer of any security incidents.
Deal Breaker: The provider is not required to notify the customer of any security incidents and is not bound by any incident response obligations.

Preferred Position: All IP developed by the vendor during the performance of the contract is assigned to the customer.
Fallback 1: All IP developed by the vendor during the performance of the contract is assigned to the customer, but the vendor retains rights to use the IP for its own purposes.
Fallback 2: All IP developed by the vendor during the performance of the contract is assigned to the customer, but the vendor may retain non-exclusive rights for internal use.
Fallback 3: All IP developed by the vendor during the performance of the contract is assigned to the customer, but the vendor may retain rights to use the IP for its own purposes.
Red Line: The vendor is not required to assign any IP developed during the performance of the contract.
Deal Breaker: The vendor is not required to assign any IP and retains all rights to any IP developed during the performance of the contract.

Preferred Position: The customer has exclusive rights to use the AI model for the agreed purpose, and the vendor may not use the model for any other purpose.
Fallback 1: The customer has exclusive rights to use the AI model for the agreed purpose, but the vendor may use the model for research and development purposes.
Fallback 2: The customer has exclusive rights to use the AI model for the agreed purpose, but the vendor may use the model for non-commercial purposes.
Fallback 3: The customer has exclusive rights to use the AI model for the agreed purpose, but the vendor may use the model for internal testing.
Red Line: The customer does not have exclusive rights to use the AI model and the vendor may use the model for any purpose.
Deal Breaker: The customer does not have exclusive rights to use the AI model and the vendor may use the model for any purpose, including commercial use.

Preferred Position: The contract term is for 12 months with automatic renewal unless terminated 60 days in advance.
Fallback 1: The contract term is for 12 months with automatic renewal unless terminated 90 days in advance.
Fallback 2: The contract term is for 12 months with automatic renewal unless terminated 180 days in advance.
Fallback 3: The contract term is for 12 months with automatic renewal unless terminated 365 days in advance.
Red Line: The contract term is for 12 months with no automatic renewal and no termination notice required.
Deal Breaker: The contract term is for 12 months with no automatic renewal and the customer may terminate the contract at any time without notice.

Preferred Position: The customer has the right to customize the software to meet its specific business needs, with no restrictions on the scope of customization.
Fallback 1: The customer has the right to customize the software to meet its specific business needs, but the vendor may impose reasonable restrictions on the scope of customization.
Fallback 2: The customer has the right to customize the software to meet its specific business needs, but the vendor may require approval for major customizations.
Fallback 3: The customer has the right to customize the software to meet its specific business needs, but the vendor may require a fee for customizations.
Red Line: The customer does not have the right to customize the software and the vendor may impose restrictions on any customizations.
Deal Breaker: The customer does not have the right to customize the software and the vendor may impose restrictions on all customizations, including internal use.

Preferred Position: The vendor must notify the customer of any data breach within 24 hours and provide a detailed report within 7 days.
Fallback 1: The vendor must notify the customer of any data breach within 48 hours and provide a detailed report within 14 days.
Fallback 2: The vendor must notify the customer of any data breach within 72 hours and provide a detailed report within 30 days.
Fallback 3: The vendor must notify the customer of any data breach within 7 days and provide a detailed report within 60 days.
Red Line: The vendor is not required to notify the customer of any data breaches.
Deal Breaker: The vendor is not required to notify the customer of any data breaches and is not bound by any breach notification obligations.

Preferred Position: The vendor may not allow any third-party access to customer data without the customer's prior written consent.
Fallback 1: The vendor may not allow any third-party access to customer data without the customer's prior written consent, but may share data with service providers for operational purposes.
Fallback 2: The vendor may not allow any third-party access to customer data without the customer's prior written consent, but may share data with service providers for operational purposes with limited access.
Fallback 3: The vendor may not allow any third-party access to customer data without the customer's prior written consent, but may share data with service providers for operational purposes with limited access and oversight.
Red Line: The vendor may allow any third-party access to customer data without the customer's consent.
Deal Breaker: The vendor may allow any third-party access to customer data without the customer's consent and is not bound by any restrictions on data sharing.

Preferred Position: Both parties agree to mutual non-disclosure of all confidential information exchanged during negotiations.
Fallback 1: Confidentiality applies only to the disclosing party's information.
Fallback 2: Confidentiality is limited to information shared in written form.
Fallback 3: Confidentiality applies only to information shared in the presence of both parties.
Red Line: Confidentiality does not apply to information shared by the other party.
Deal Breaker: No confidentiality obligations apply to either party.

Preferred Position: The service provider must comply with all applicable data protection laws and regulations.
Fallback 1: The service provider will comply with data protection laws in the jurisdiction where the data is processed.
Fallback 2: The service provider will comply with data protection laws in the jurisdiction of the client.
Fallback 3: The service provider will comply with data protection laws in the jurisdiction of the service provider.
Red Line: The service provider is not required to comply with data protection laws.
Deal Breaker: No data protection obligations apply to the service provider.

Preferred Position: The AI model developed by the vendor is owned by the client upon payment of the final milestone.
Fallback 1: The AI model is owned by the client upon completion of the project.
Fallback 2: The AI model is owned by the client upon acceptance of deliverables.
Fallback 3: The AI model is owned by the client upon receipt of the final deliverable.
Red Line: The AI model is owned by the vendor unless otherwise agreed in writing.
Deal Breaker: The AI model is owned by the vendor and cannot be transferred to the client.

Preferred Position: All IP developed during the engagement is owned by the client.
Fallback 1: All IP developed during the engagement is owned by the client unless otherwise agreed in writing.
Fallback 2: All IP developed during the engagement is owned by the client, with appropriate attribution.
Fallback 3: All IP developed during the engagement is owned by the client, with a right of use granted to the vendor.
Red Line: The vendor retains ownership of all IP developed during the engagement.

Preferred Position: The software must comply with all applicable security standards and certifications.
Fallback 1: The software must comply with the most relevant security standards and certifications.

Preferred Position: The contract term is limited to a maximum of three years with automatic renewal options.

Preferred Position: All IP developed during the engagement is assigned to the client upon payment of the final milestone.

Fallback 2: All IP developed during the engagement is assigned to the client upon acceptance of deliverables.
Fallback 3: All IP developed during the engagement is assigned to the client upon receipt of the final deliverable.

Preferred Position: The vendor may use the client's data solely for the purpose of providing the AI service.

Fallback 2: The vendor may use the client's data for the purpose of providing and improving the AI service.

Preferred Position: The client may terminate the engagement with 30 days' written notice.

Preferred Position: Both parties agree to mutual non-disclosure with defined scope and duration.

Preferred Position: Data is processed in compliance with GDPR and CCPA standards.
